question: Which country's deaf cricket team won a historic 5-match series against Trinidad & Tobago in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Deaf Cricket Team** created history by winning a **5-match series** against **Trinidad & Tobago** in early **2025**.
 
• This tour was a landmark event as it represented the first time an **Indian Deaf Cricket** squad traveled to the **West Indies** for a bilateral international series.
 
• The series was played in the **T20 format**, and the **Indian** team showcased a dominant performance throughout the matches held at various venues in **Trinidad**, including the **National Cricket Centre** in **Couva**.
 
• The tour was organized and facilitated by the **Indian Deaf Cricket Association (IDCA)** in collaboration with the **Trinidad and Tobago Deaf Cricket Association** and the **Trinidad and Tobago Cricket Board**.
 
• The victory highlights the growing prowess of **differently-abled athletes** from **India** on the global stage and serves as a significant boost for the sport's visibility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Deaf Cricket Association (IDCA):**
 
 
• The **IDCA** is the governing body for deaf cricket in **India**, focused on promoting the sport among hearing-impaired individuals.
 
• It is led by President **Sumit Jain** and has been instrumental in organizing national championships and international tours to provide exposure to **Indian** talent.
 
• The association aims for formal recognition from the **BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India)** to further professionalize the sport for the deaf community.
 
 
 
• **International Achievements:**
 
 
• Prior to the **2025** series win, **India** had already established itself as a major contender, notably winning the **DICC (Deaf International Cricket Council) T20 Champions Trophy** in **2022**.
 
• The **2025** series victory against **Trinidad & Tobago** serves as critical preparation for future global events like the **Deaf Cricket World Cup**.
 
 
 
• **Deaf Cricket Dynamics:**
 
 
• The game follows the standard **ICC (International Cricket Council)** rules for **T20** and **ODI** formats, but with specific adaptations for communication.
 
• Umpires often use **colored flags** in addition to standard hand signals to communicate decisions to the players who cannot hear the sound of the whistle or the ball hitting the bat.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Tour:**
 
 
• International tours like the one to **Trinidad & Tobago** promote **social inclusion** and provide a platform for athletes to represent **India** globally.
 
• Such events help in attracting **sponsorships** and government support for **para-sports**, which is essential for the long-term sustainability of deaf cricket.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Location:** The historic series took place in the **Caribbean** nation of **Trinidad & Tobago**, known for its rich cricketing heritage.
 
• **Format:** The matches were specifically **T20 Internationals**, which is the most popular format for deaf cricket due to its fast-paced nature.
 
• **Year:** The series was successfully concluded in **January-February 2025**.
 
• **Inclusivity:** The success of the team is often celebrated as a part of the broader **"Khelo India"** spirit, encouraging sports participation across all sections of society, including those with physical impairments.
